home.trajectoryDesc: Bullets don't fly straight. Here's exactly how far off — drop, windage, velocity, time of flight, at any distance.

trajectory.title: Trajectory
trajectory.spinDriftUnavailable: Spin drift could not be calculated.

bcEstimate.intro: Enter a near velocity and range, then either a far velocity or a measured time of flight to the far range, plus a drag model and atmosphere, to back out the ballistic coefficient that explains the observed change. If you have a choice, use residual velocity rather than time of flight — this is typically more precise.
bcEstimate.errorNearRangeExceedsFar: Near distance must be less than far distance.

bcTools.title: BC Tools
bcTools.intro: Calculate BC from known data, convert between different models, etc.
bcTools.invalidTof: Enter a valid time of flight (a positive number of seconds).

bcConversion.intro: Convert a ballistic coefficient from one standard drag model to another, at a single reference velocity. The conversion is exact at that velocity, and drifts the further your bullet's actual velocity strays from it — pick a velocity representative of the range band you care about.

bcToolsLabradar.intro: This tool only works with tracks from a Labradar v1 device (the big orange box). Upload a Labradar chronograph export (a .zip of track files) to fit a ballistic coefficient per shot, then average across the valid ones. Files that aren't real tracks — the device's own report or project files, or unrelated junk that ended up in the zip — are ignored automatically.
bcToolsLabradar.filterR2HintNone: Do not reject tracks based on fit quality.
bcToolsLabradar.filterR2HintHighNoise: Use if you run the radar in a particularly noisy environment (obstacles in or near the line of fire) and see too many valid measurements rejected.
bcToolsLabradar.filterSigmaHintNone: Disable if you are very sure of your data (single shooter, good conditions, radar well aligned to the target) — especially for small datasets of fewer than 10 shots.
bcToolsLabradar.filterSigmaHintConservative: Recommended default — rejects tracks whose BC is more than 2× the standard deviation from the mean, e.g. a shot picked up from a nearby lane.
bcToolsLabradar.filterSigmaHintAggressive: Rejects more aggressively — useful on a busy range with similar calibers nearby, or without realigning between targets. May also discard some valid data, reducing accuracy.
bcToolsLabradar.denoiseHint: Leave at 0.990 (Normal), unless you are operating in a very noisy environment and are losing too many valid data points.
bcToolsLabradar.chartEmptyHint: Select a track below to see its velocity-vs-time curve.
bcToolsLabradar.emptyBatchError: No track files were found in that zip.

cdMachCurve.title: Cd–Mach Curve
cdMachCurve.intro: Paste a distance/velocity table (e.g. Doppler radar or multi-chronograph readings) to back out this bullet's own drag curve, segment by segment.
cdMachCurve.tableInstructions: One pair per line: distance, then velocity, separated by tab, space or semicolon. Decimal point or comma both work.
cdMachCurve.tableRecommendationHint: Aim for consecutive velocities at least ~20 m/s (~65 fps) apart — narrower segments are extended automatically, but tightly bunched readings still add more rounding noise than real resolution. If the table's velocities never drop well below Mach 1.0 (~340 m/s / ~1125 fps), it stays entirely supersonic and won't capture any transonic behavior — a standard G1/G7 model with a BC estimated over Mach 2.5–1.5 (~850 m/s / ~2790 fps down to ~510 m/s / ~1675 fps) will likely serve you better (see BC Tools).
cdMachCurve.tableErrorTooFewRows: Enter at least 3 distance/velocity pairs, one per line.
cdMachCurve.tableErrorBadLine: Line {{line}}: expected a distance and a velocity, separated by tab, space or semicolon.
cdMachCurve.errorMassCaliberRequired: Enter the bullet's mass and caliber first.
cdMachCurve.skippedSegmentsWarning: {{count}} segment(s) skipped (see below) — the rest of the table is unaffected.
cdMachCurve.skipReasonNonDecreasingVelocity: velocity didn't decrease between these two rows
cdMachCurve.skipReasonNotConverged: solver didn't converge for this segment
cdMachCurve.skipReasonNonPositiveCd: solver hit a non-physical drag coefficient for this segment

multiBc.intro: Turn 2-5 manufacturer-published BC values, each valid over its own speed band, into a bullet-specific Cd-Mach curve — drag the segment borders on the chart, or type them into the table below it.
multiBc.massCaliberHint: Mass and caliber both directly affect the resulting curve and the optimal BC values below — enter them accurately.
multiBc.chartHint: Click the chart to add a segment border, drag a border to move it, click × on a border to remove it.
multiBc.maxSegmentsHint: A maximum of {{max}} segments is supported.
multiBc.errorFromExceedsTo: This value must be strictly between its own segment's neighboring borders.
multiBc.optimalBcHint: A single BC per model that best approximates this bullet's own supersonic behavior, computed between Mach {{startMach}} (muzzle) and Mach {{endMach}} (the beginning of the transonic band), in standard sea-level atmosphere.
multiBc.optimalBcUnreachable: No BC value for this model reproduces this bullet's supersonic behavior within the usual range.

hitProbability.title: Hit Probability
hitProbability.intro: Probability of hitting a target for a chosen firing scenario, given your rifle and load, accounting for your own precision and the conditions of the shot.
hitProbability.syncHint: Same selection as on the Trajectory page — picking a rifle or bullet here updates it there too.
hitProbability.simplifiedHint: This value represents the combined precision of rifle, cartridge, and shooter in your typical shooting position.
hitProbability.battleZeroToggleLabel: Battle zero (rifle zeroed at a different range)
hitProbability.contributionHeadingSighting: Contribution to total error - sighting shot
hitProbability.contributionHeadingCorrected: Contribution to total error - corrected shot

rangeSolverLocations.title: Locations & Targets
rangeSolverLocations.intro: Save a shooting location's targets once, then pick them straight from the Target tab on later visits — wind and atmosphere are never part of this, only range, angle and where each target is.
rangeSolverLocations.noLocationOption: No location — single target, manual entry
rangeSolverLocations.notPlacedBadgeTitle: Not yet placed on the location photo
rangeSolverLocations.altitudeHint: Optional. If set, making this location active fills in the Atmosphere tab with the standard atmosphere at this altitude and 50% humidity — but only if you haven't already changed atmosphere values yourself this session.
rangeSolverLocations.photoHint: Attach a photo taken from the shooting position to quickly pick a target visually, instead of a name list.
rangeSolverLocations.cropHint: Drag the corners to crop the photo, or leave them at the edges to use the whole photo.
rangeSolverLocations.photoProcessingError: Could not process that photo. Please try a different file.
rangeSolverLocations.duplicateNameWarning: A location with this name already exists — saving will overwrite it.
rangeSolverLocations.duplicateTargetNameWarning: Another target at this location already has this name.
rangeSolverLocations.targetNameHint: Optional — leave blank to use "Target 1", "Target 2", etc.
rangeSolverLocations.pinFieldHint: Tap the photo to place this target's pin, drag it to fine-tune, pinch to zoom, drag empty space to pan.
rangeSolverLocations.importFileErrorInvalidFormat: That file isn't a recognized Locations library export.
rangeSolverLocations.photoOverlayHint: Tap a target to select it.

riflePrecision.title: Rifle Precision Calculator
riflePrecision.intro: Photograph a paper target, mark the point of aim and every bullet hole, and get real precision numbers — extreme spread, group centroid, and pooled statistics once you're ready — across as many targets and groups as you like.
riflePrecision.unusableBadgeTitle: Missing calibration, point of aim, or an impact — this target cannot be analyzed
riflePrecision.cropHint: Drag the corners to crop the photo, or leave them at the edges to use the whole photo.
riflePrecision.photoProcessingError: Could not process that photo. Please try a different file.
riflePrecision.calibrationHint1: Tap the photo at the first calibration point — one end of a ruler or a known-length feature on the target.
riflePrecision.calibrationHint2: Tap the photo at the second calibration point, then enter the real-world distance between the two points.
riflePrecision.poaHint: Tap the photo to place this group's point of aim.
riflePrecision.shotHint: Tap the photo to record each bullet hole — keep tapping to add more.
riflePrecision.deleteImpactHint: Tap the impact you want to remove, or Cancel to keep it.
riflePrecision.idleHint: Pick a group below to keep adding shots to it, or add a new group.
riflePrecision.noShotsToAnalyzeHint: There is nothing to analyse yet. Mark some shots first.
riflePrecision.impactsToScaleHint: Draws each impact at the bullet's true bore diameter instead of a fixed marker size. Switch off for visual clarity, if there is too much overlap between the impacts (precise rifle at short distance).
riflePrecision.duplicateNameWarning: An entry with this name already exists in your Rifle Precision library — saving will overwrite it.
riflePrecision.importFileErrorInvalidFormat: That file doesn't look like a Rifle Precision export.
riflePrecision.r50Description: Circular error probable, the radius of a circle where 50% of impacts are expected to fall
riflePrecision.r95Description: The radius of a circle where 95% of impacts are expected to fall
riflePrecision.r99Description: The radius of a circle where 99% of impacts are expected to fall

settings.title: Settings
settings.intro: Choose a preferred unit for each kind of measurement — mix metric and imperial freely. These apply everywhere that measurement appears across the tools and are remembered on this device.
settings.zeroForSpinDriftLabel: Account for spin drift when zeroing
settings.dragModelsHint: Hide standard drag models you don't use, to declutter the drag-model picker. A hidden model stays available wherever it's already selected — hiding it never changes an existing choice.
settings.csvSeparatorHint: Should be different from each other, or spreadsheet software may not read the file correctly.

releaseHistory.title: Release history
releaseHistory.intro: What's changed in each release of this app.

entries.v156: Bugfix: offline functionality (some tools failed to run offline, if never used online before).
entries.v155: New user setting: range solver output units, special delivery for our click-impaired friends.
entries.v154: The 'high speed low drag' range solver just got more awesomer — everything key is in a single pane now, no more clicking back and forth. Also, a version bump and a new release code name (because I thought of a cool one).
entries.v153: Feature to crop images on import. Increased image quality (resolution and lossy compression factor).
entries.v152: The THANKS page is no longer a stub.
entries.v151: New awesome wind input widget design.
entries.v150: A mess with two 7mm calibers sorted out — now properly separated into 6.8 and 7 proper. Props to ForgeValley for raising it.
entries.v149: Nice round range defaults for yards (when selected) in Trajectory and Hit Probability.
entries.v148: Icons and layout tweaks to improve PWA mode on iOS and Android.
entries.v147: Added a "loading" indicator on application start-up.
entries.v146: Engine upgrade to 4-DOF / MPM. Spin drift calculations implemented by McCoy's equations. McCoy's transverse moment of inertia constant (corresponding to .308 168gr SMK projectile) replaced by length-to-caliber-dependent function fit, calibrated with Lapua 6-DOF data.
entries.v145: Bugfix: fixed how the Range Solver's distance and wind speed inputs handle non-metric units — rounding and step size. (Props to 6.5SH.) Feature: added a "U/D, L/R" option for the Range Solver's output indicators (not translated).
entries.v144: The last of the tools has been ported to the new suite platform: meet the Rifle Precision Calculator (formerly known as Taran) – perhaps the most controversial, offensive, ego-shattering, pride-wounding, humiliating, demoralizing, and butthurt-inducing piece of software I've ever written. There's also automatic migration of Locations data from the old storage back-end to the new one, some UI polishing, and an update to the user manual reflecting everything that's happened since v136 (2.2). All this mandates a major version bump, and an awesome new version codename.
entries.v143: Implemented IndexedDB storage back-end, and migrated Locations data storage to it.
entries.v142: New unit setting – wind speed – separate from the general velocity, and used for all wind inputs across the project.
entries.v141: Range solver moved out to its own top-level navigation entry. Mobile presentation adjusted to accommodate one more icon.
entries.v140: Implemented a tool to convert multi-BC to custom curve (and to single optimal BC). Ever since Sierra realized we live in the third millennium, the tool is less useful than it used to be, but you never know who would want to be unique next.
entries.v139: Added a "Hornady reverse radar" built-in bullets library, with a few bullets I actually care for (more to come).
entries.v138: Unit-related UI fixes / accessibility features for our metric-impaired friends.
entries.v137: Bugfix: some UI elements ignored weird user unit preferences, and defaulted to metric.
entries.v136: Support of multiple built-in bullet libraries, individually switchable for display. Import of Lapua radar measured Cd-Mach curves as "Lapua Cd" lib. Minor UI enhancements.
entries.v135: Input validation / sanity checks implemented all over the app. Arsenal entry UI reworked to make it (hopefully) clearer, and (certainly) awesomer.
entries.v134: The Range Solver is final, with a beautiful (optional) feature to save target data for a location, and pick your targets directly from a photo taken from the shooter's position. Major polishing of mobile interface, to make portrait and landscape modes display correctly on various devices. All this mandates a major version bump, and an awesome new version codename.
entries.v133: Range Solver: a summary conditions bar was added above the elevation and windage readout, showing target range, wind, and atmosphere at a glance.
entries.v132: BC Tools is complete: BC Conversion now converts a ballistic coefficient between standard drag models at a chosen reference velocity, live as you type. BC Tools no longer shows as Partial.
entries.v131: Minor UI clarifications and bug fixes.
entries.v130: First public release. Since the last update: Labradar BC fitting now solves the whole velocity-vs-time window against the physics model directly, instead of a per-pair linear fit, paired with a tighter default de-noise threshold. UI improvements.
entries.v129: Added the Labradar tool to BC Tools: upload a Labradar chronograph export (a .zip of track files) to fit a BC per shot, with the same noise-cleaning approach as the original standalone tool, adjustable signal-quality and outlier filters, and a velocity-vs-time chart per track.
entries.v128: UI cosmetics: the wind-angle dial on Trajectory is now 1.75x larger, and it's centered together with its manual-degrees entry within the field.
entries.v127: Added six more standard drag models (G2, G5, G6, G8, GI, GS) alongside G1/G7, corrected G7's own table at high Mach numbers, and added a Settings toggle to show or hide individual models — G1 and G7 stay visible by default, the rest are opt-in.
entries.v126: Merged the BC Estimator, BC — Time of Flight, and BC — Labradar Track tools into one BC Tools page with Calculation, Conversion, and Labradar tabs — switch between a measured far velocity or a time-of-flight reading, and your entries now persist when you navigate away and back.
entries.v125: Fixed a bug where changing the comparison chart's max distance in Arsenal (or Trajectory) could blank the chart and leave the zoom sliders stuck on "NaN".
entries.v124: Cd-Mach Curve is live: paste a Doppler radar or chronograph distance/velocity table and back out the bullet's own drag curve, segment by segment. Chart it against G1/G7, export the tables, and save the result straight to Arsenal.
entries.v123: The Hit Probability tool is now a target-rich environment. Migrated all targets from legacy Plan 33 code, stand by for more scenarios.
entries.v122: Cosmetic changes / interface polishing for public release. Great thanks to S.E. for thorough review and feedback of v104, driving most changes implemented since then.
entries.v121: On mobile, Range Solver's Wind tab now sizes its direction dial to fit the screen and hides the manual degree entry (the dial itself stays fully operable, including by keyboard).
entries.v120: Trajectory calculations now interpolate between simulation steps with a quadratic (3-point) fit instead of linear, reducing the small residual error at in-between ranges.
entries.v119: Added a separate unit preference for rifling twist rate (mm or inches), independent of the sight-height/aim-offset unit choice.
entries.v116: Added bullet stability (Miller) and spin drift (Litz) calculations, removed the "example" rifles and bullets from the built-in library, gave every built-in rifle its rifling twist, and added release history with update notifications (can be turned off in Settings).
